It is a risky business to write an entire scene in which the actors are upstaged by the silence of the hilarious stream of comments from a Live Screen session projected on the school library’s back wall.
Eureka Day took a societal phenomenon that I find intimidating, and lovingly reminded me that, in a ridiculous world, it’s okay to take a moment to laugh at how outrageous our extremes really are.
Eureka Day is the funniest play of the year.

cn.t: Critics praise this sharp satire of progressive Berkeley parents debating vaccines as one of Broadway's funniest offerings, with a standout Zoom chat scene earning mid-show applause, though some find its barbs feel dated post-pandemic.

vs.sum: The Samuel J. Friedman Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions and a well-raked mezzanine, ensuring a clear view from most seats. The sound quality is consistently praised, and the seating is comfortable with decent legroom. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant design following renovation, though facilities like restrooms are average, leading to some congestion during intermissions.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Built-in induction loop for t-coil hearing aids.
